name: Lysosomal Storage Disease with Skeletal Involvement

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Lysosomal Storage Disease Diagnostic Criteria with Skeletal Involvement

criteria.description: Demonstration of deficient lysosomal enzyme activity in leukocytes or fibroblasts
Presence of characteristic skeletal abnormalities on radiographic imaging (dysostosis multiplex)
Identification of pathogenic mutation(s) in lysosomal enzyme or transporter gene
Presence of clinical features such as joint stiffness, short stature, and skeletal deformities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Deficient lysosomal enzyme activity plus either characteristic skeletal radiographic abnormalities or identification of pathogenic genetic mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires integration of biochemical, genetic, and radiological data.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic constellation of skeletal abnormalities seen on imaging

pathognomonic.symptomName: Joint stiffness with limited range of motion
Short stature due to skeletal dysplasia
searchTerms: short height caused by bone growth disorders
below average stature due to skeletal issues
kidney problems with protein in urine

laboratory: Reduced lysosomal enzyme activity in leukocytes or fibroblasts
Elevated urinary glycosaminoglycans or storage material
Abnormal lysosomal storage products in biopsy specimens
imaging: Radiographic evidence of dysostosis multiplex including thickened ribs, oar-shaped ribs, and vertebral anomalies
MRI showing brain atrophy or white matter changes in some cases
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in genes encoding lysosomal enzymes or transport proteins (e.g., IDUA, GLB1, GUSB)
other: Histopathology showing lysosomal storage in affected tissues

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly skeletal involvement with corneal clouding absent
Normal lysosomal enzyme activity for other LSDs
Absence of coarse facial features and corneal clouding

redFlags: Progressive joint contractures and skeletal deformities in early childhood
references: Neufeld EF, Muenzer J. The mucopolysaccharidoses. In: The Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease. 8th ed. McGraw-Hill; 2001.
